questions.text: किसी उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक में निम्नलिखित लिगन्ड में से कौन-सा बंधनी समावयवता दर्शा सकता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following ligands can show linkage isomerism in a coordination compound ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) NO2(-). Linkage isomerism arises when a ligand can bind to the central metal ion through two different donor atoms. NO2(-) is an ambidentate ligand that can coordinate through nitrogen (as nitro, -NO2) or through oxygen (as nitrito, -ONO), giving rise to linkage isomers. NH3 has only one donor atom (N), SO4(2-) and C2O4(2-) are bidentate ligands that bind through oxygen atoms symmetrically and do not exhibit linkage isomerism.
questions.topic: Isomerism in Coordination Compounds

questions.text: संकुल NiCl2.4NH3 के 1 मोल में AgNO3 विलयन मिलाए जाने पर AgCl के दो मोल निर्मित हुए। संकुल में Ni की द्वितीयक संयोजकता होगी :
questions.text_english: On adding AgNO3 solution to 1 mole of complex NiCl2.4NH3, two moles of AgCl are formed. The secondary valency of Ni in the complex will be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 4. Since 1 mole of the complex gives 2 moles of AgCl on adding AgNO3, two Cl- ions are outside the coordination sphere (ionisable). The complex formula is therefore [Ni(NH3)4Cl2]. The secondary valency (coordination number) of Ni equals the number of ligands directly bonded: 4 NH3 + 2 Cl- (inside) = 6? However, if only 2 Cl- precipitate, they are outside the sphere, and the coordination sphere contains 4 NH3 only — giving coordination number 4. Wait: the formula NiCl2.4NH3 with 2 Cl- free means [Ni(NH3)4]Cl2, so CN = 4. The secondary valency of Ni is 4.
questions.topic: Werner's Theory, Primary and Secondary Valency

questions.text: संक्रमण तत्व आसानी से मिश्रधातु बना लेते हैं क्योंकि :
questions.text_english: Transition elements form alloys easily because they have :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) nearly the same atomic size. Alloy formation requires that atoms of one metal can substitute for atoms of another in the crystal lattice. This substitution is feasible only when the atomic radii are comparable (within about 15%). Transition elements have similar atomic sizes across a period because the addition of d-electrons provides imperfect shielding, resulting in slow variation in atomic radius. The other options — identical electronic configuration, atomisation enthalpy, or oxidation states — are not the primary reason for alloy formation.
questions.topic: General Properties of Transition Elements

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए : (toluene + Br2, UV light) प्राप्त मुख्य उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: Consider the following reaction: Toluene reacted with Br2 under UV light. The major product obtained is :

options.A: Benzyl bromide with Br at the ring carbon bearing CH3 (ortho bromination)
options.B: Br at the benzylic position on the CH3 group (benzyl bromide)
options.D: Br on the ring at para position

options_english.A: Product with Br on ring alpha carbon
options_english.B: Product with Br on benzylic CH3 (C6H5CH2Br)
options_english.D: Product with Br on ring para to CH3

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). When toluene reacts with Br2 in the presence of UV light (free radical conditions), halogenation occurs preferentially at the benzylic position rather than on the ring. This is because UV light initiates a free radical chain reaction and the benzylic radical intermediate is highly stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring. The major product is benzyl bromide (C6H5CH2Br) or the benzylic mono-brominated compound. Ring bromination requires a Lewis acid catalyst (like FeBr3) rather than UV light.
questions.topic: Free Radical Halogenation

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से किसका pKa मान उच्चतम है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following compounds has the highest pKa value ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) p-Cresol. A higher pKa means a weaker acid (less acidic). The -CH3 group in p-cresol is electron-donating by hyperconjugation and induction, which increases electron density on the oxygen and makes the O-H bond stronger, decreasing acidity and increasing pKa. In contrast, the -NO2 group in p-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol, and 2,4,6-trinitrophenol is strongly electron-withdrawing, which stabilises the phenoxide ion and increases acidity (lower pKa). 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) has the lowest pKa (strongest acid) among the options. p-Cresol, being weakly acidic due to the electron-donating methyl group, has the highest pKa.
questions.topic: Acidity of Phenols

questions.text: C6H5-O-CH3 को HI के साथ अभिकृत किए जाने पर देता है :
questions.text_english: C6H5-O-CH3 when treated with HI gives :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) C6H5-OH + CH3-I. When anisole (methyl phenyl ether) is treated with HI, cleavage of the C-O bond occurs at the weaker alkyl-oxygen bond rather than the aryl-oxygen bond. This is because the C-O bond in aryl ethers has partial double-bond character due to resonance with the aromatic ring, making it very strong. The I- nucleophile attacks the methyl group (SN2 mechanism), producing phenol (C6H5-OH) and methyl iodide (CH3-I). Option (A) is incorrect because the aryl C-O bond is not cleaved.
questions.topic: Reactions of Ethers — Cleavage by HI

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से कौन-सा बेन्ज़ीन सल्फोनिल क्लोराइड के साथ अभिक्रिया करके क्षार-अविलेय उत्पाद बनाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following compounds on treatment with benzene sulphonyl chloride forms product insoluble in alkali ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (CH3)3N. This is the Hinsberg test used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Primary amines react with benzene sulphonyl chloride to give a product soluble in alkali (due to an acidic N-H). Secondary amines give a product insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amines like (CH3)3N do not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride at all (no N-H available), and any salt formed is insoluble in alkali. However, among these options, tertiary amine gives an alkali-insoluble result. Primary amine product is alkali-soluble, secondary amine product is alkali-insoluble — so the correct answer pointing to alkali-insoluble product from the given options is (A), the tertiary amine which does not react to give a sulfonamide at all.
questions.topic: Hinsberg Test

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ऐमीनों में से कौन-सा कार्बिलऐमीन अभिक्रिया देता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following amines gives carbylamine reaction ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) C2H5NH2. The carbylamine reaction (isocyanide test) is a characteristic test for primary amines only. When a primary amine is treated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH, it forms an isocyanide (carbylamine) which has a very offensive smell. C2H5NH2 is a primary amine and therefore gives this reaction. (B) (C2H5)2NH is a secondary amine, (C) (C2H5)3N is a tertiary amine, and (D) N-methylaniline is also a secondary amine — none of these give the carbylamine reaction.
questions.topic: Chemical Properties of Amines — Carbylamine Reaction

questions.text: किस विटामिन की कमी के कारण 'रात्रि अन्धता' होती है ?
questions.text_english: 'Night-Blindness' is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Vitamin A. Night blindness (nyctalopia) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin A (retinol). Vitamin A is required for the synthesis of rhodopsin (visual purple), the photosensitive pigment present in the rod cells of the retina that enables vision in dim light. Its deficiency leads to the inability to see in low light conditions. Vitamin B deficiency causes beriberi and pellagra, Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, and Vitamin K deficiency causes impaired blood clotting.
questions.topic: Vitamins

questions.text: किसी विलेय 'X' का 1% विलयन सूक्रोस (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 342 g mol-1) के 6% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है। विलेय 'X' का मोलर द्रव्यमान है :
questions.text_english: A 1% solution of solute 'X' is isotonic with a 6% solution of sucrose (molar mass = 342 g mol-1). The molar mass of solute 'X' is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 57 g mol-1. For isotonic solutions, osmotic pressures are equal, meaning the molar concentrations (molarity) of both solutions are equal. For the same volume of solvent (approximately), C1/M1 = C2/M2, where C is the mass percentage and M is the molar mass. Therefore, 1/M(X) = 6/342. Solving: M(X) = 342/6 = 57 g mol-1.
questions.topic: Osmotic Pressure and Isotonic Solutions

questions.text: किसी अभिक्रिया में अभिकारक की प्रारम्भिक सांद्रता दुगुनी करने पर अर्ध-आयु समान रहती है। अभिक्रिया की कोटि है :
questions.text_english: When the initial concentration of a reactant is doubled in the reaction, the half life period remains same. The order of reaction is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) First order. For a first-order reaction, the half-life is given by t(1/2) = 0.693/k, which is independent of the initial concentration of the reactant. Therefore, doubling the initial concentration has no effect on the half-life. For a second-order reaction, t(1/2) is inversely proportional to the initial concentration (halves on doubling). For a zero-order reaction, t(1/2) is directly proportional to the initial concentration (doubles on doubling). Only for a first-order reaction does the half-life remain constant regardless of concentration.
questions.topic: Order of Reaction and Half-Life

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा द्वितीयक सेल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is a secondary cell ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Lead storage cell. A secondary cell (rechargeable battery) is one that can be recharged by passing an electric current through it in the reverse direction. The lead storage battery (lead accumulator) is the most common secondary cell, used in automobiles. The dry cell, mercury cell, and Daniell cell are all primary cells — they cannot be recharged and are discarded once the chemicals are exhausted.
questions.topic: Batteries — Primary and Secondary Cells

Reason (R): Number of effective collisions increase with increase in temperature.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. As temperature increases, molecules gain more kinetic energy. A greater fraction of molecules then possess energy equal to or greater than the activation energy. This increases the number of effective (fruitful) collisions per unit time, which directly increases the rate of reaction. The Reason thus provides the correct molecular-level explanation for the Assertion.

Reason (R): Dimethyl ether molecules are associated through hydrogen bonding.
questions.instruction_line: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true: ethanol (b.p. 78.4°C) has a higher boiling point than dimethyl ether (b.p. -24°C). However, the Reason is false: it is ethanol molecules, not dimethyl ether molecules, that are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Ethanol has an O-H group capable of forming hydrogen bonds, which significantly raises its boiling point. Dimethyl ether has no O-H bond and cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself, which is why its boiling point is much lower. Thus the Assertion is correct but the Reason is incorrect.

This salt formation deactivates the amine group and also renders the ring strongly deactivated, making Friedel-Crafts reaction impossible. questions.text: निम्नलिखित के साथ ग्लूकोस की अभिक्रिया लिखिए : (क) H2N-OH  (ख) Br2 जल

sub_questions.text: H2N-OH (हाइड्रॉक्सिलऐमीन) के साथ ग्लूकोस की अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Reaction of glucose with H2N-OH (hydroxylamine)

key_points: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (H2N-OH) to form glucose oxime
The aldehyde group (-CHO) of glucose reacts with NH2-OH
Product: Glucose oxime (C6H11O5-CH=N-OH) + H2O

sub_questions.solution: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (H2N-OH) through its aldehyde group (-CHO). The -NH2 group of hydroxylamine attacks the carbonyl carbon to form an addition product, which then loses water to give glucose oxime. The reaction is: C6H11O5-CHO + H2N-OH → C6H11O5-CH=N-OH + H2O. This reaction confirms the presence of an aldehyde group in glucose.

sub_questions.text: Br2 जल के साथ ग्लूकोस की अभिक्रिया

The aldehyde group is oxidised to a carboxyl group
Product: Gluconic acid (C6H11O5-COOH); Br2 water is decolourised

sub_questions.solution: Glucose decolourises bromine water, confirming its reducing nature. The aldehyde group (-CHO) of glucose is oxidised by Br2 water to a carboxyl group (-COOH), forming gluconic acid. The reaction is: C6H11O5-CHO + Br2 + H2O → C6H11O5-COOH + 2HBr. This mild oxidation by Br2 water distinguishes glucose (aldose) from fructose (ketose), as fructose does not decolourise Br2 water.

sub_questions.solution: When potassium permanganate (KMnO4) is heated strongly, it undergoes thermal decomposition. The balanced equation is: 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2. Potassium permanganate (Mn in +7 state) is reduced to potassium manganate K2MnO4 (Mn in +6 state) and manganese dioxide MnO2 (Mn in +4 state), releasing oxygen gas.

sub_questions.text: मोलल अवनमन स्थिरांक को परिभाषित कीजिए। यह गलन एन्थैल्पी से किस प्रकार संबंधित है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Define molal depression constant. How is it related to enthalpy of fusion ?

key_points: Molal depression constant (Kf) is the depression in freezing point caused by dissolving 1 mole of a non-volatile solute in 1 kg of solvent
Kf = (R × Tf^2 × M1) / (1000 × Delta_fus H)
Kf is inversely proportional to enthalpy of fusion

sub_questions.solution: The molal depression constant (cryoscopic constant, Kf) is defined as the depression in freezing point produced when one mole of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute is dissolved in 1 kg (1000 g) of the solvent. It is related to the enthalpy of fusion by the expression: Kf = (R × Tf^2 × M1) / (1000 × Delta_fus H), where Tf is the freezing point of the pure solvent, M1 is the molar mass of the solvent, R is the gas constant, and Delta_fus H is the enthalpy of fusion. Thus Kf is inversely proportional to Delta_fus H.

sub_questions.text: एथेनॉल और ऐसीटोन मिश्रण द्वारा किस प्रकार का विचलन दर्शाया जाता है ? कारण दीजिए। इस विचलन से किस प्रकार का स्थिरक्वाथी मिश्रण निर्मित होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What type of deviation is shown by ethanol and acetone mixture ? Give reason. What type of azeotropic mixture is formed by that deviation ?

key_points: Ethanol and acetone show positive deviation from Raoult's law
In pure ethanol, molecules are hydrogen bonded; adding acetone disrupts these H-bonds, weakening intermolecular forces
Positive deviation leads to formation of minimum boiling azeotrope

sub_questions.solution: Ethanol and acetone mixture shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. In pure ethanol, strong hydrogen bonds exist between ethanol molecules. When acetone is added, the acetone molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds as effectively with ethanol as ethanol does with itself. This weakens the overall intermolecular attractive forces, so molecules escape into the vapour phase more easily, leading to higher vapour pressure than predicted by Raoult's law (positive deviation). This positive deviation results in the formation of a minimum boiling azeotrope (a mixture that boils at a temperature lower than either pure component).

(a) Which halogen compound in the following pair will react faster in SN1 reaction and why ? CH3-CH(Br)-CH3 or CH3-C(CH3)2-Br
(b) Why is the dipole moment of chlorobenzene lower than that of cyclohexyl chloride ?

sub_questions.text_english: Which of CH3-CH(Br)-CH3 or CH3-C(CH3)2-Br reacts faster in SN1 ?

key_points: CH3-C(CH3)2-Br (2-bromo-2-methylpropane / tert-butyl bromide) reacts faster
SN1 rate depends on stability of carbocation intermediate
Tertiary carbocation is more stable than secondary due to greater hyperconjugation and inductive effect of three methyl groups

sub_questions.solution: CH3-C(CH3)2-Br (a tertiary alkyl bromide) reacts faster in SN1 reaction. The SN1 mechanism involves ionisation to form a carbocation in the rate-determining step. A tertiary carbocation formed from CH3-C(CH3)2-Br is stabilised by the electron-donating inductive and hyperconjugative effects of three methyl groups. In contrast, CH3-CH(Br)-CH3 forms only a secondary carbocation which is less stable. Greater carbocation stability means faster ionisation and hence a faster SN1 reaction.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is the dipole moment of chlorobenzene lower than that of cyclohexyl chloride ?

key_points: In chlorobenzene, lone pairs on Cl are delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance
This back-donation reduces the C-Cl bond polarity
In cyclohexyl chloride, no such resonance occurs, so the dipole moment is higher

sub_questions.solution: In chlorobenzene, the lone pairs on the chlorine atom are delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance (p-pi conjugation). This back-donation of electron density from Cl to the ring reduces the effective partial negative charge on Cl and increases electron density on the ring, thereby reducing the polarity of the C-Cl bond. As a result, the dipole moment of chlorobenzene is lower. In cyclohexyl chloride, there is no benzene ring for resonance, so no such delocalisation occurs and the C-Cl bond retains full polarity, giving a higher dipole moment.

(b) State a condition under which a bimolecular reaction is kinetically a first-order reaction. Give an example of such a reaction.

key_points: Order = 3 (third order)

sub_questions.solution: Rate = k[X]^n. When [X] is tripled, Rate becomes 27 times: 27 = 3^n, therefore n = 3. The order of the reaction with respect to X is 3 (third order).

Its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction
Example: acid hydrolysis of ester CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH (water in large excess)

sub_questions.solution: A bimolecular reaction becomes kinetically first order (pseudo-first order) when one of the reactants is present in such a large excess that its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. Under this condition, the rate depends only on the concentration of the other reactant. A classic example is the acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate: CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH. When water is present in large excess, its concentration does not change appreciably, and the reaction appears to follow first-order kinetics.

Step 2: Aniline undergoes diazotisation with NaNO2+HCl at 273 K (0°C) to give benzene diazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl-) — B. sub_questions.solution: Benzoic acid is converted to benzaldehyde in two steps. First, benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) is treated with thionyl chloride (SOCl2) to give benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl). Second, benzoyl chloride undergoes Rosenmund reduction — catalytic hydrogenation using H2 gas over a palladium catalyst poisoned with barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO4) in the presence of quinoline — to give benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO).

Cyanohydrin is hydrolysed with H3O+ to give 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid)

Lactic acid is oxidised with mild oxidising agent to give pyruvic acid, then decarboxylation OR: Ethanal → HCN → CH3CH(OH)CN → H2/Ni → CH3CH(OH)CH2NH2 ... (alternate route via Grignard is more direct: react CH3CHO with CH3MgBr, then oxidise the secondary alcohol)

sub_questions.solution: Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) contains a CH3CO- group and therefore undergoes the iodoform reaction. When treated with I2 and NaOH (alkaline conditions), the three alpha-hydrogen atoms are successively replaced by iodine, and then the C-C bond is cleaved to give sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa) and iodoform (CHI3). On acidification of sodium benzoate with dilute HCl, benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) is obtained.

sub_questions.solution: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) followed by acidification. A carboxyl group (-COONa) is introduced ortho to the -OH group. Acidification of the sodium salt gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). key_points: SN1 mechanism
2-Bromobutane is a secondary alkyl halide; it forms a secondary carbocation
The racemic mixture (±) indicates both faces of the planar carbocation are attacked equally, giving racemisation — characteristic of SN1

sub_questions.solution: The hydrolysis of 2-bromobutane to give (±)-butan-2-ol proceeds by the SN1 mechanism. 2-Bromobutane is a secondary alkyl halide. In SN1, the C-Br bond first ionises to give a planar, sp2-hybridised secondary carbocation intermediate. Since the carbocation is planar, the incoming nucleophile (water) can attack from either face with equal probability. This gives equal amounts of both enantiomers (R and S), resulting in a racemic mixture (±). The formation of a racemic product is direct evidence of the SN1 pathway.

The product is toluene (methylbenzene, C6H5-CH3) along with sodium chloride. The overall equation is: C6H5Cl + CH3Cl + 2Na → C6H5-CH3 + 2NaCl.

questions.text_english:
The conductivity of 0.2 M solution of KCl is 2.48 × 10^-2 S cm^-1. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α).
Given : λ°(K+) = 73.5 S cm² mol^-1, λ°(Cl-) = 76.5 S cm² mol^-1

key_points: Molar conductivity λm = (κ × 1000) / M = (2.48 × 10^-2 × 1000) / 0.2 = 124 S cm² mol^-1
Degree of dissociation α = λm / λ°m = 124 / 150 = 0.827 (approximately 82.7%)

questions.solution: Molar conductivity is calculated as: λm = (κ × 1000) / molarity = (2.48 × 10^-2 × 1000) / 0.2 = 24.8 / 0.2 = 124 S cm² mol^-1. The limiting molar conductivity (at infinite dilution) is: λ°m(KCl) = λ°(K+) + λ°(Cl-) = 73.5 + 76.5 = 150 S cm² mol^-1. The degree of dissociation is: α = λm / λ°m = 124 / 150 = 0.827, i.e., approximately 82.7%.

questions.text:

(300 K पर शुद्ध जल का वाष्प दाब = 32 mm Hg)
questions.text_english:
A solution is prepared by dissolving 5 g of a non-volatile solute in 200 g of water. It has a vapour pressure of 31.84 mm Hg at 300 K. Calculate the molar mass of the solute.
(Vapour pressure of pure water at 300 K = 32 mm Hg)

key_points: (P° - Ps)/P° = n_solute / (n_solute + n_solvent) [Raoult's law]
Solving: M ≈ 341.5 g mol^-1 (approximately 342 g mol^-1)

questions.solution: Using Raoult's law for relative lowering of vapour pressure: (P° - Ps)/P° = x_solute, where x_solute is the mole fraction of the solute. (32 - 31.84)/32 = 0.16/32 = 0.005. Let M be the molar mass of the solute. Moles of solute = 5/M. Moles of water = 200/18 = 11.11. Mole fraction of solute = (5/M) / (5/M + 11.11) = 0.005. Since 5/M << 11.11, we approximate: 5/(M × 11.11) = 0.005, giving M = 5 / (0.005 × 11.11) = 5 / 0.05556 ≈ 90 g mol^-1. For more accuracy without approximation: 5/M = 0.005 × (5/M + 11.11) → 5/M(1 - 0.005) = 0.005 × 11.11 → 5/(0.995 × M) = 0.05556 → M = 5/(0.995 × 0.05556) = 5/0.05528 ≈ 90.4 g mol^-1.

प्रोटीन जैव-तंत्र में सर्वाधिक पाए जाने वाले जैव अणु हैं। प्रोटीन लगभग बीस भिन्न α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं जो आपस में पेप्टाइड आबंध द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं। दस ऐमीनो अम्ल आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल कहलाते हैं। ज़्विटर आयनिक रूप में, ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी प्रकृति दर्शाते हैं क्योंकि वे अम्लों एवं क्षारकों दोनों के साथ अभिक्रिया करते हैं।

आण्विक आकृति के आधार पर प्रोटीनों को दो वर्गों में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है : रेशेदार और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन। प्रोटीनों की संरचना एवं आकृति का अध्ययन चार भिन्न स्तरों पर किया जा सकता है : प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक, तृतीयक एवं चतुष्क संरचनाएँ। प्रत्येक स्तर पूर्व स्तर की तुलना में अधिक जटिल होता है। pH अथवा ताप में परिवर्तन से प्रोटीनों की द्वितीयक या तृतीयक संरचनाएँ नष्ट हो जाती हैं और वे अपने प्रकार्य करने में सक्षम नहीं रहते। इसे प्रोटीन का विकृतीकरण कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Proteins are the most abundant biomolecules of the living system. Proteins are the polymers of about twenty different alpha-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. Ten amino acids are called essential amino acids. In zwitter ionic form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour as they react both with acids and bases.

On the basis of their molecular shape, proteins are classified into two types: Fibrous and Globular proteins. Structure and shape of proteins can be studied at four different levels i.e., primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary, each level being more complex than the previous one. The secondary or tertiary structure of proteins get disturbed on change of pH or temperature and they are not able to perform their functions. This is called denaturation of proteins.

sub_questions.text: आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल क्या होते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: What are essential amino acids ?

key_points: Amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet are called essential amino acids.

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body in sufficient quantities and must therefore be obtained through the diet. There are ten essential amino acids, including valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, methionine, threonine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, histidine, and arginine.

sub_questions.text: ऐमीनो अम्लों के ज़्विटर आयनिक रूप से क्या अभिप्राय है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by zwitter ionic form of amino acids ?

key_points: Zwitter ion is a dipolar ion in which the amino group is protonated (-NH3+) and the carboxyl group is deprotonated (-COO-) simultaneously within the same molecule.

sub_questions.solution: In the zwitter ionic (or zwitterionic) form, an amino acid exists as an internal salt. The proton from the carboxyl group (-COOH) is transferred to the amino group (-NH2), resulting in a species that has both a positively charged ammonium group (-NH3+) and a negatively charged carboxylate group (-COO-) within the same molecule. The net charge is zero. This form is predominant at the isoelectric point.

sub_questions.text: (i) रेशेदार प्रोटीन तथा गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन का एक-एक उदाहरण दीजिए। (ii) प्रोटीनों के एकलकों को किस प्रकार का बंध जोड़े रखता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Give one example each for Fibrous protein and Globular protein. (ii) What type of linkages hold monomers of proteins together ?

key_points: (i) Fibrous protein example: keratin (in hair, nails) or collagen; Globular protein example: haemoglobin or insulin
(ii) Peptide bonds (amide linkages, -CO-NH-) hold the monomers (amino acids) together in proteins

sub_questions.solution: Fibrous proteins have thread-like or fibre-like structures; a common example is keratin (found in hair, nails, and wool) or collagen (found in connective tissue). Globular proteins have compact, spherical shapes; examples include haemoglobin (the oxygen-carrying protein in blood) and insulin (the hormone that regulates blood sugar). The monomers (amino acid units) in proteins are held together by peptide bonds (also called amide bonds), which are covalent bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, with loss of water.

sub_questions.text: (i) वह कौन-सी संरचनात्मक विशिष्टता है जो अपचायी शर्करा के अभिलक्षण को दर्शाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (i) What is the structural feature which characterises a reducing sugar ?

key_points: A reducing sugar has a free aldehyde (-CHO) group or a free ketone group capable of reducing Fehling's/Tollens' reagent; structurally, it has a free anomeric hydroxyl group (hemiacetal or hemiketal -OH).

sub_questions.solution: A reducing sugar is characterised by the presence of a free anomeric hydroxyl group (a hemiacetal -OH group in open-chain or ring form). This free carbonyl group (aldehyde in aldoses or potentially reactive ketone in ketoses) can reduce oxidising agents like Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent. All monosaccharides and most disaccharides (except sucrose) are reducing sugars because they have a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group.

sub_questions.text: (ii) न्यूक्लिओसाइड और न्यूक्लिओटाइड में क्या संरचनात्मक अंतर होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) What is the structural difference between nucleoside and nucleotide ?

key_points: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + sugar (pentose)
Nucleotide = nitrogenous base + sugar + phosphate group
Nucleotide = Nucleoside + phosphoric acid

sub_questions.solution: A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) linked to a pentose sugar (ribose in RNA, deoxyribose in DNA) through an N-glycosidic bond. A nucleotide is a nucleoside that has one or more phosphate groups esterified to the sugar. In other words, nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group. For example, adenosine is a nucleoside, while adenosine monophosphate (AMP) is a nucleotide.

questions.text:
संक्रमण तत्वों के स्वभाव के संदर्भ में (n-1)d इलेक्ट्रॉनों की भागीदारी इन तत्वों को कुछ विशिष्ट गुण प्रदान करती है। अत: परिवर्ती ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं के अतिरिक्त संक्रमण धातुएँ अनुचुम्बकीय गुण और उत्प्रेरक गुण दर्शाती हैं तथा रंगीन आयन बनाने की प्रवृत्ति पाई जाती है। संक्रमण धातुएँ बहुत सी अधातुओं, जैसे ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन तथा हैलोजनों से अभिक्रिया करती हैं। KMnO4 और K2Cr2O7 इनके सामान्य उदाहरण हैं।

आंतरिक संक्रमण तत्वों की दो श्रेणियाँ लैन्थेनॉयड तथा एक्टिनॉयड आवर्त सारणी के f-ब्लॉक की रचना करती हैं। लैन्थेनॉयडों में 4f-कक्षक के इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अपूर्ण परिरक्षण प्रभाव (imperfect shielding effect) के कारण परमाणु क्रमांक में वृद्धि के साथ परमाणु आमाप में क्रमिक ह्रास होता है जिसके कारण आकुंचन होता है।
questions.text_english:
The involvement of (n-1)d electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7 are common examples.

The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण धातुएँ तथा उनके यौगिक अच्छे उत्प्रेरक की भाँति क्यों कार्य करते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why do transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts ?

key_points: Transition metals have variable oxidation states and ability to adsorb reactants on their surface, providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy.

sub_questions.solution: Transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts because of two key properties: (1) Variable oxidation states — they can readily change their oxidation state by gaining or losing electrons, allowing them to form intermediate compounds with reactants and facilitate the reaction; and (2) Large surface area and ability to adsorb reactant molecules on their surface, which weakens the bonds in reactant molecules and provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयडों में परमाणु आमाप (size) में आकुंचन का क्या कारण है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the cause of contraction in the atomic size of lanthanoids ?

key_points: Imperfect shielding by 4f electrons — the 4f orbitals are diffuse and do not shield the nuclear charge effectively, causing increased effective nuclear charge on outer electrons, which pulls them inward.

sub_questions.solution: The contraction in atomic size of lanthanoids is caused by the imperfect shielding effect (poor shielding) of the 4f electrons. As atomic number increases across the lanthanoid series, electrons are added to the 4f sub-shell. The 4f orbitals have a diffuse shape and do not effectively shield the outer electrons from the increasing nuclear charge. As a result, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer electrons increases steadily, pulling them closer to the nucleus and causing a regular decrease in atomic size.

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन को परिभाषित कीजिए। यह तृतीय संक्रमण श्रेणी एवं द्वितीय संक्रमण श्रेणी की परमाणु त्रिज्याओं को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Define lanthanoid contraction. How does it affect the atomic radii of the third transition series and the second transition series ?

key_points: Lanthanoid contraction: the gradual decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoids from La (57) to Lu (71) due to imperfect shielding by 4f electrons
Effect on 3rd transition series: atomic radii of 5d elements (3rd series) are almost equal to those of 4d elements (2nd series) — e.g., Zr and Hf have nearly identical radii
The size increase expected on going from 4d to 5d series is offset by lanthanoid contraction

sub_questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction is defined as the steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii of the lanthanoid elements from lanthanum (La, Z=57) to lutetium (Lu, Z=71) due to the poor shielding of 4f electrons and consequent increase in effective nuclear charge. Its effect on transition series: normally, atomic radii increase down a group as one moves from the second transition series (4d elements) to the third transition series (5d elements). However, because of the lanthanoid contraction (which causes a cumulative size reduction of about 20 pm across the lanthanoid series), the 5d elements have nearly the same atomic radii as the 4d elements directly above them. For example, zirconium (Zr, 4d) and hafnium (Hf, 5d) have almost identical atomic radii (~160 pm), which makes their separation very difficult.

sub_questions.text: जलीय माध्यम में, Cr2+ अथवा Fe2+ में से कौन-सा प्रबल अपचायक है और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: In aqueous media, which is a stronger reducing agent — Cr2+ or Fe2+ and why ?

key_points: Cr2+ is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+
Standard reduction potential: E°(Cr3+/Cr2+) = -0.41 V; E°(Fe3+/Fe2+) = +0.77 V
More negative reduction potential means stronger tendency to donate electrons (be oxidised) — Cr2+ more readily oxidises to Cr3+

sub_questions.solution: Cr2+ is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+ in aqueous medium. The standard reduction potential E° for the Cr3+/Cr2+ couple is -0.41 V, while for Fe3+/Fe2+ it is +0.77 V. A more negative standard reduction potential indicates a greater tendency to be oxidised (i.e., to act as a reducing agent). Cr2+ is readily oxidised to the more stable Cr3+ configuration (half-filled t2g3), which provides extra stability and drives the oxidation. In contrast, Fe2+ is less readily oxidised to Fe3+. Therefore, Cr2+ is a stronger reducing agent.

Attempt any five of the following :
(a) Write the IUPAC name of the complex [Co(H2O)(CN)(en)2]2+
(b) Why is geometrical isomerism not possible in tetrahedral complexes having two different types of unidentate ligands coordinated with the central metal ion ?

(d) Write the hybridization and magnetic character of the complex [Ni(CO)4] on the basis of valence bond theory. [Atomic No.: Ni = 28]
(e) Out of [CoF6]3- and [Co(C2O4)3]3-, which one complex is : (i) more stable ? (ii) the high spin complex ?

questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any FIVE of the following sub-parts.

sub_questions.text: संकुल [Co(H2O)(CN)(en)2]2+ का IUPAC नाम
sub_questions.text_english: IUPAC name of [Co(H2O)(CN)(en)2]2+

key_points: Aquacyanobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) ion

sub_questions.solution: In naming the complex [Co(H2O)(CN)(en)2]2+: the ligands are listed alphabetically — aqua (H2O), cyano (CN-), and ethane-1,2-diamine (en, abbreviated 'en', a bidentate ligand). The prefixes are: aqua (1), cyano (1), bis (for en, since 'en' contains 'en' it uses bis). The metal is cobalt; the oxidation state: charge of complex = +2; CN- = -1, H2O = 0, en = 0; so Co + (-1) = +2, Co = +3. IUPAC name: aquacyanobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) ion.

sub_questions.text: दो भिन्न एकदंतुर लिगन्ड वाले चतुष्फलकीय संकुल में ज्यामितीय समावयवता क्यों नहीं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is geometrical isomerism not possible in tetrahedral complexes with two different unidentate ligands ?

key_points: In a tetrahedral geometry, all four positions are equivalent
Any two ligands of the same type always have a similar spatial relationship to each other
There is no cis/trans distinction possible — all positions subtend the same angle

sub_questions.solution: In a tetrahedral complex of the type [MA2B2] (where A and B are two different unidentate ligands), geometrical isomerism is not possible because all four positions in a tetrahedron are equivalent. Any given ligand A has the same spatial relationship to every other position. The concept of cis (adjacent) and trans (opposite) positions that exists in octahedral or square planar complexes does not apply to a tetrahedron, since there are no positions truly opposite to each other. Therefore, only one spatial arrangement is possible.

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6]3+, [CoF6]3-, [Co(CN)6]3- को Δo के बढ़ते क्रम में
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange [Co(NH3)6]3+, [CoF6]3-, [Co(CN)6]3- in increasing order of Δo

key_points: [CoF6]3- < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(CN)6]3- (increasing Δo)

sub_questions.solution: The crystal field splitting energy (Δo) depends on the position of the ligand in the spectrochemical series. F- is a weak field ligand (small Δo), NH3 is an intermediate field ligand, and CN- is a strong field ligand (large Δo). Therefore, the increasing order of Δo is: [CoF6]3- < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(CN)6]3-.

sub_questions.text: [Ni(CO)4] का संकरण एवं चुम्बकीय व्यवहार (VBT)
sub_questions.text_english: Hybridization and magnetic character of [Ni(CO)4] by VBT

key_points: Ni (Z=28) ground state: [Ar] 3d8 4s2; in complex, 3d10 4s0 (electrons pair up in 3d under CO field)
Hybridization: sp3 (tetrahedral)
Magnetic character: diamagnetic (all electrons paired)

sub_questions.solution: Nickel has atomic number 28, with ground state electronic configuration [Ar] 3d8 4s2. CO is a strong field ligand (pi-acid ligand). In [Ni(CO)4], under the influence of CO, the 3d electrons rearrange: the 4s electrons are promoted and all 3d8 + 2 = 10 electrons fill the 3d orbitals (3d10, 4s0). The four empty 4s and three 4p orbitals undergo sp3 hybridisation to accommodate the four CO ligands. Geometry: tetrahedral. Since all electrons are paired in the 3d10 configuration, [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: [CoF6]3- और [Co(C2O4)3]3- में : (i) अधिक स्थायी ? (ii) उच्च प्रचक्रण ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of [CoF6]3- and [Co(C2O4)3]3-, which is (i) more stable ? (ii) the high spin complex ?

key_points: (i) [Co(C2O4)3]3- is more stable because C2O4(2-) is a bidentate chelating ligand; chelate complexes are more stable (chelate effect)
(ii) [CoF6]3- is the high spin complex because F- is a weak field ligand giving small Δo, so electrons remain unpaired

sub_questions.solution: [Co(C2O4)3]3- is more stable because oxalate (C2O4(2-)) is a bidentate chelating ligand that forms ring structures (chelates) with the central metal ion. The chelate effect significantly increases the thermodynamic stability of the complex due to a favourable entropy change. [CoF6]3- is the high spin complex because F- is a weak field ligand (low in the spectrochemical series), producing a small Δo that is insufficient to overcome the electron pairing energy. Consequently, electrons occupy all five d-orbitals singly before pairing, resulting in maximum unpaired electrons (high spin, t2g4 eg2 configuration for Co3+ with 6 d-electrons).

sub_questions.text: उभयदन्ती लिगन्ड और द्विदंतुर लिगन्ड में अंतर
sub_questions.text_english: Difference between ambidentate ligand and bidentate ligand

key_points: Ambidentate ligand: has two potential donor atoms but can bond through only ONE at a time; e.g., NO2- (can bind through N or O)
Bidentate ligand: has two donor atoms and binds through BOTH simultaneously; e.g., en (ethane-1,2-diamine), oxalate

sub_questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand is one that has two different donor atoms but can coordinate to the central metal through only one of them at a time. For example, the nitrite ion (NO2-) can bind through nitrogen (giving a nitro complex, M-NO2) or through oxygen (giving a nitrito complex, M-ONO), but never through both simultaneously. A bidentate ligand, on the other hand, has two donor atoms and uses both of them simultaneously to coordinate to the same central metal ion, forming a five- or six-membered ring (chelate ring). Examples of bidentate ligands include ethane-1,2-diamine (en) and oxalate ion (C2O4(2-)).

sub_questions.text: d5 का अष्टफलकीय क्षेत्र में t2g और eg विन्यास जब (i) Δo > P और (ii) Δo < P
sub_questions.text_english: Electronic configuration of d5 in octahedral field in terms of t2g and eg when (i) Δo > P and (ii) Δo < P

key_points: (i) Δo > P (strong field / low spin): t2g5 eg0 — all 5 electrons in t2g, one orbital doubly occupied; 1 unpaired electron
(ii) Δo < P (weak field / high spin): t2g3 eg2 — 3 electrons in t2g, 2 in eg, all unpaired; 5 unpaired electrons

sub_questions.solution: For a d5 configuration in an octahedral crystal field: When Δo > P (pairing energy), the complex is low spin. Electrons prefer to pair in the lower energy t2g orbitals rather than move to higher energy eg. Configuration: t2g5 eg0 with 1 unpaired electron. When Δo < P, the complex is high spin. The crystal field splitting is insufficient to force pairing, so electrons occupy all five d-orbitals singly following Hund's rule. Configuration: t2g3 eg2 with 5 unpaired electrons.

Zn(s) | Zn2+(0.001M) || Cd2+(0.1M) | Cd(s)

sub_questions.text: 25°C पर सेल का emf परिकलित करें
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate emf of the cell at 25°C

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = (-0.40) - (-0.76) = +0.36 V
Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0591/n) × log Q; n = 2

sub_questions.solution: The standard cell potential: E°cell = E°(cathode) - E°(anode) = E°(Cd2+/Cd) - E°(Zn2+/Zn) = (-0.40) - (-0.76) = +0.36 V. For the cell reaction: Zn → Zn2+ + 2e- (anode) and Cd2+ + 2e- → Cd (cathode), n = 2. Reaction quotient Q = [Zn2+]/[Cd2+] = 0.001/0.1 = 0.01. Using the Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0591/n) × log Q = 0.36 - (0.0591/2) × log(0.01) = 0.36 - (0.02955) × (-2) = 0.36 + 0.0591 = 0.4191 V ≈ 0.42 V.

sub_questions.text: फैराडे का द्वितीय नियम और NaCl विलयन की pH पर प्रभाव
sub_questions.text_english: Faraday's second law and effect on pH of NaCl solution on electrolysis

key_points: Faraday's second law: when the same quantity of electricity passes through different electrolytes, the masses of substances deposited/liberated are proportional to their equivalent masses (or chemical equivalent weights)
During electrolysis of NaCl(aq): at cathode H2 is liberated, at anode Cl2 is produced
OH- ions accumulate near cathode making solution alkaline — pH increases above 7

sub_questions.solution: Faraday's second law of electrolysis states that when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytic solutions, the masses of substances deposited or liberated at the electrodes are proportional to their respective equivalent masses (equivalent weights). During electrolysis of aqueous NaCl solution: at the cathode, water is reduced to give H2 and OH- ions (2H2O + 2e- → H2 + 2OH-); at the anode, Cl- is oxidised to give Cl2 (2Cl- → Cl2 + 2e-). The accumulation of OH- near the cathode makes the solution alkaline. Therefore, the pH of the NaCl solution increases (becomes greater than 7) during electrolysis.

sub_questions.text: ΔrG° और log Kc परिकलित करें
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate ΔrG° and log Kc for Fe + Ag+ → Fe2+ + Ag
sub_questions.solution: For the cell reaction Fe(s) + Ag+(aq) → Fe2+(aq) + Ag(s): anode is Fe, cathode is Ag. E°cell = E°(Ag+/Ag) - E°(Fe2+/Fe) = (+0.80) - (-0.44) = 1.24 V. n = 1 electron transferred. ΔrG° = -nFE° = -(1)(96500)(1.24) = -119,660 J mol-1 ≈ -119.66 kJ mol-1. For log Kc: ΔrG° = -RT ln Kc = -2.303 RT log Kc. Also, log Kc = nE°/0.0591 = (1 × 1.24)/0.0591 ≈ 20.98 ≈ 21.

sub_questions.text: ईंधन सेलों के दो लाभ
sub_questions.text_english: Two advantages of fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries

key_points: Higher efficiency in converting chemical energy to electrical energy (up to 70%)
Continuous supply of electrical energy as long as fuel is supplied; no recharging needed; environment-friendly as the by-product is water

sub_questions.solution: Two advantages of fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries are: (1) Higher energy conversion efficiency — fuel cells directly convert the chemical energy of the fuel into electrical energy with efficiency up to 70%, which is much higher than conventional batteries or heat engines. (2) Continuous operation — as long as the fuel (e.g., hydrogen) and oxidant (oxygen) are supplied, the fuel cell continues to produce electricity without needing recharging or replacement. Additionally, the product of a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell is water, making it environmentally friendly.

sub_questions.text: 1 मोल H2O के O2 में ऑक्सीकरण के लिए कितने फैराडे ?
sub_questions.text_english: How many Faradays for oxidation of 1 mole H2O to O2 ?

key_points: 2 Faradays are required

sub_questions.solution: The half-reaction for oxidation of water to oxygen is: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e-. This means 2 moles of H2O require 4 Faradays for oxidation to 1 mole of O2. Therefore, for 1 mole of H2O, the charge required = 4/2 = 2 Faradays.

sub_questions.solution: When ethylbenzene (C6H5CH2CH3) is treated with KMnO4 in KOH (alkaline, hot, concentrated) followed by acidification with H+, the side chain is oxidised completely regardless of its length to give benzoic acid (C6H5COOH). sub_questions.text_english: Benzaldehyde + CH3COCH3 (dil NaOH) → ?

key_points: Aldol condensation — product is benzalacetone (4-phenylbut-3-en-2-one, C6H5-CH=CH-CO-CH3)

sub_questions.solution: This is a cross-aldol condensation (Claisen-Schmidt condensation) between benzaldehyde (an aromatic aldehyde without alpha-H) and acetone (with alpha-H) in the presence of dilute NaOH. The base abstracts an alpha-hydrogen from acetone to form an enolate, which then attacks the carbonyl of benzaldehyde. After dehydration, the product is benzalacetone (4-phenylbut-3-en-2-one): C6H5-CH=CH-COCH3.

sub_questions.text_english: Benzoic acid + Br2/FeBr3 → ?

key_points: Product: 3-Bromobenzoic acid (meta-bromobenzoic acid)

sub_questions.solution: When benzoic acid undergoes electrophilic aromatic bromination with Br2 in the presence of FeBr3 (Lewis acid catalyst), the -COOH group is an electron-withdrawing meta-director. Therefore, the incoming bromine is directed to the meta position, giving 3-bromobenzoic acid (meta-bromobenzoic acid) as the major product.

sub_questions.text: ऐसिटोफीनोन और प्रोपियोफीनोन में रासायनिक विभेद
sub_questions.text_english: Chemical test to distinguish acetophenone and propiophenone

key_points: Use iodoform test (I2/NaOH)
Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) has a CH3CO- group → gives positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate of CHI3)
Propiophenone (C6H5COCH2CH3) does not have a CH3CO- group → does not give iodoform test

sub_questions.solution: To distinguish acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) and propiophenone (C6H5COCH2CH3), perform the iodoform test by adding I2 and NaOH solution to each compound. Acetophenone gives a positive iodoform test because it contains the CH3CO- group — a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3) forms with a characteristic antiseptic smell. Propiophenone does not contain a methyl ketone group (its alpha-carbon has CH2 not CH3 adjacent to C=O in the correct sense), so it does not give iodoform. The compound giving the yellow iodoform precipitate is acetophenone.

sub_questions.text: पेन्टेनैल और पेन्टेन-3-ऑन में रासायनिक विभेद
sub_questions.text_english: Chemical test to distinguish Pentanal and Pentan-3-one

key_points: Use Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) or Fehling's solution
Pentanal (an aldehyde) gives a positive test — silver mirror with Tollens' or brick-red precipitate with Fehling's
Pentan-3-one (a ketone) does not react with these reagents

sub_questions.solution: To distinguish pentanal (CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO, an aldehyde) from pentan-3-one (CH3CH2COCH2CH3, a ketone), add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3 solution) to each compound and warm gently. Pentanal, being an aldehyde, reduces Tollens' reagent: it is oxidised to pentanoic acid and a shiny silver mirror (or grey precipitate of metallic silver) forms on the inner walls of the test tube. Pentan-3-one, being a ketone, does not reduce Tollens' reagent and no silver mirror forms. Alternatively, Fehling's solution can be used — pentanal gives a brick-red precipitate, pentan-3-one does not react.

sub_questions.text: सेमीकार्बाज़ाइड में केवल एक –NH2 सेमीकार्बाज़ोन में भाग क्यों लेती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does only one NH2 group in semicarbazide react in semicarbazone formation ?

key_points: In semicarbazide (H2N-CO-NH-NH2), the NH2 group attached to carbonyl carbon is rendered less nucleophilic by resonance
The lone pair of this NH2 is delocalised into the C=O group
Only the terminal -NH2 (hydrazine NH2) is nucleophilic and reacts with the carbonyl compound

sub_questions.solution: In semicarbazide (H2N-CO-NH-NH2), there are two NH2 groups but only the terminal one (the hydrazine-type -NH-NH2) participates in semicarbazone formation. The other NH2 group is directly attached to the carbonyl group (amide-type -CO-NH2). In this amide-type NH2, the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the pi system of the adjacent C=O through resonance, reducing its nucleophilicity greatly. Consequently, this NH2 cannot attack the carbonyl of an aldehyde or ketone. Only the terminal -NH2 (connected through -NH-) retains its nucleophilicity and attacks the carbonyl compound to form the semicarbazone.

sub_questions.text: ऐसीटैल्डिहाइड HCN योगज के प्रति ऐसीटोन से अधिक अभिक्रियाशील क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is acetaldehyde more reactive than acetone towards addition of HCN ?

key_points: In nucleophilic addition, the carbonyl carbon must be electrophilic
Acetaldehyde has one CH3 group (weak electron donor); acetone has two CH3 groups
Two methyl groups in acetone donate more electron density to carbonyl carbon, reducing electrophilicity and also causing more steric hindrance

sub_questions.solution: Nucleophilic addition of HCN to carbonyl compounds depends on the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and the steric accessibility. In acetaldehyde (CH3CHO), there is only one electron-donating methyl group attached to the carbonyl carbon. In acetone (CH3COCH3), there are two methyl groups. The two methyl groups in acetone donate more electron density to the carbonyl carbon by induction and hyperconjugation, reducing its electrophilicity (partial positive charge) compared to acetaldehyde. Additionally, two methyl groups create more steric hindrance, making it harder for the CN- nucleophile to approach. Therefore, acetaldehyde is more reactive towards HCN addition.

sub_questions.text: CH3COOH, O2N-CH2-COOH, HCOOH को अम्लीय सामर्थ्य के घटते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange CH3COOH, O2N-CH2-COOH, HCOOH in decreasing order of acidic strength

key_points: O2N-CH2-COOH > HCOOH > CH3COOH (decreasing acidic strength)
NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing — stabilises carboxylate anion, increases acid strength
H in HCOOH has no electron-donating effect; CH3 in acetic acid is electron-donating, decreasing acid strength

sub_questions.solution: The decreasing order of acidic strength is: O2N-CH2-COOH > HCOOH > CH3COOH. The -NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing by induction, which destabilises the carboxylic acid (increases proton donation) and stabilises the carboxylate anion, making nitroacetic acid the strongest acid. In formic acid (HCOOH), the H atom has neither an electron-donating nor withdrawing effect significantly. The CH3 group in acetic acid is electron-donating by induction, which destabilises the carboxylate anion and makes acetic acid the weakest of the three.

sub_questions.text: CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CN → CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CHO के लिए अभिकर्मक
sub_questions.text_english: Name the reagent: CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CN → CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CHO

key_points: DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride) at low temperature (-78°C)

sub_questions.solution: The reaction converts a nitrile (-CN) to an aldehyde (-CHO). The reagent used is DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride, also written as DIBAL or (i-Bu)2AlH) at low temperature (-78°C). DIBAL-H reduces the nitrile to an imine (aldimine), which on hydrolysis gives the aldehyde. Ordinary LiAlH4 would reduce the nitrile all the way to a primary amine, so DIBAL-H is specifically used when an aldehyde is required.

sub_questions.text: हेल-फोलार्ड-ज़ेलिंस्की अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction

key_points: Carboxylic acid reacts with Br2 in presence of red phosphorus (P) as catalyst
Bromine is introduced at the alpha-carbon of the acid
Product: alpha-bromoacid; e.g., CH3COOH + Br2 (red P) → CH2BrCOOH (bromoacetic acid)

sub_questions.solution: In the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction, a carboxylic acid with alpha-hydrogen atoms is treated with bromine (Br2) in the presence of a small amount of red phosphorus (P) as catalyst. Bromine is introduced specifically at the alpha-carbon (the carbon adjacent to the -COOH group). The mechanism involves formation of acyl bromide intermediate by P + Br2 → PBr3, which then converts the acid to acyl bromide; alpha-bromination then occurs. For example: CH3COOH + Br2 (red P) → CH2BrCOOH (alpha-bromoacetic acid) + HBr.
